title: Burnley, Middlesbrough and West Ham in contention for Robert Snodgrass
trail: Burnley, Middlesbrough and West Ham are in contention to sign Robert Snodgrass after Hull named their price for the Scotland international
body: Burnley, Middlesbrough and West Ham United are in contention to sign Robert Snodgrass after Hull named their price for the Scotland international. Having previously rejected a number of offers for the 29-year-old, Hull finally relented on Wednesday morning when Burnley submitted a bid of an initial £7.5m with up to £2.5m in bonuses. That has yet to be matched by either Middlesbrough or West Ham, although it understood they have indicated they would be willing to slightly improve their offers of £7m plus £3m in bonuses to land the player who has scored seven goals in the Premier League this season. A number of other clubs including Crystal Palace, Watford, Swansea, Sunderland and Bournemouth have also registered an interest, although it remains to be seen whether they follow that up with an official bid. Should that happen, the decision will be left to Snodgrass and his representatives to agree personal terms before he allowed to leave the Kcom Stadium. It is believed that the former Norwich City and Leeds United winger favours a move to either Middlesbrough or West Ham, with Burnley unlikely to be able to match his wage demands, with the player having previously turned down the offer of £4m a season after tax to move to the Chinese Super League. Snodgrass refused to sign a three-year contract last month, although Hull recently instigated a one-year contract extension that means he is tied to the club until the summer of 2018. Having already signed Oumar Niasse and Lazar Markovic on loan, Hull’s manager Marco Silva has also made an approach to sign the Ivory Coast forward Nicolas Pépé from French side Angers. An offer on an initial €9m (£7.7m) was submitted on Wednesday, although they face competition from Watford for the 21-year-old who has previously been linked to Everton, Liverpool and Newcastle.
